result:
I've written the review to `review.md`. Summary of the verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

Two high-severity findings, both confirmed by tracing the actual code paths:

1. **`ledger-lib.sh:157`** — the "lighter" content check (`jq empty`) accepts concatenated multi-document JSON, which the old `jq -es 'length==1 and object'` check rejected. I verified locally that feeding such input through the subsequent `.last_updated = $ts` stamping step produces two separate JSON objects, silently corrupting the ledger on write instead of erroring — reintroducing the exact bug class the guard's own comment says it exists to prevent.

2. **`check-no-swallowed-jq.sh:138-146`** — the simplified heredoc-skipper unconditionally skips *all* heredoc bodies, dropping the old distinction between executable heredocs (`bash <<EOF`) and inert documentation ones (`cat <<'EOF'`). This blinds the tripwire to the swallowed-jq anti-pattern when it appears inside an executable heredoc — the same silent-clean-gate failure mode (KF-004/KF-015) the scanner exists to catch.

Two lower-severity observations: the `printf` → `echo` swap in ledger-lib.sh, and the removed `ValueError` handler in the agy adapter (likely breaks the "never crash the fallback chain" contract, but I couldn't confirm the caller behavior since only touched files were provided).
